name_en: Tanba kuromame gohan — rice cooked with Tanba black soybeans
summary_ja: 丹波篠山特産の丹波黒大豆を米と一緒に炊き込むと、豆の色素が溶け出してほんのり紫がかったご飯になる。かつては田植え前の祈願行事で神棚や田にも供えられていたという、粒の大きく甘みの強い黒豆を生かした一品。
summary_en: Rice cooked with Tanba-Sasayama's prized black soybeans, whose pigment bleeds out to tint the grains faintly purple. It is said the dish was once offered to a household shrine and left in the paddies during a rite praying for the rice seedlings to take.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Tofumeshi — mashed tofu, canned mackerel, and root vegetables steamed into rice
summary_ja: ゆでてつぶした豆腐に鯖の水煮缶やゴボウ、ニンジンを甘辛く炒め、炊きたてのご飯に混ぜ込む丹波篠山・大山地区の混ぜご飯。寄り合いの支度を簡単にしようと、長老の発案で生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: A mixed rice dish from the Oyama district of Tanba-Sasayama, made by simmering mashed tofu with canned mackerel, burdock, and carrot in a sweet soy seasoning, then folding it into freshly steamed rice. It is said to have been devised by a village elder to simplify preparing food for community gatherings.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Tororo gohan — grated mountain yam over rice, eaten to settle the stomach
summary_ja: すりおろした山の芋をだし汁でのばし、ご飯にかけて食べる丹波篠山の一品。消化を助けるとされ、正月料理で疲れた胃を休めるため一月二日に食べる習わしが伝わる。そばのつなぎやお好み焼きに使うこともある。
summary_en: Grated mountain yam thinned with dashi and poured over rice, a Tanba-Sasayama dish said to aid digestion. A custom survives of eating it on January 2nd to rest the stomach after New Year's feasting, and the grated yam is sometimes worked into soba dough or okonomiyaki batter too.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Tako meshi — rice cooked with octopus and dashi
summary_ja: 淡路島から東播磨にかけて水揚げされるマダコを米と一緒に炊き込むご飯。夏場に旬を迎え、明石海峡の潮流にもまれた身は歯ごたえと甘みが増すとされ、生ダコのほか煮ダコや干しダコを使う地域もある。
summary_en: Rice cooked with octopus landed anywhere from Awaji Island to eastern Harima. The octopus is in season through summer, and flesh tumbled by the currents of the Akashi Strait is said to gain in both bite and sweetness; some areas use it raw, others boiled or sun-dried first.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
